notes: §1985:X.2.5.3 SR1: the END PROGRAM program-name 'must conform to the rules for forming a user-defined word', i.e. §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 'not more than 30 characters', letters, digits and the hyphen, the hyphen not first or last, at least one letter, no reserved word. endProgramHeader takes programName (cobolWord), so a literal or an all-digit name is a parse refusal (COBOL5506); VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitCobolWord applies CobolWordRule.MaxLength(1985)=30 (COBOL1567) and the reserved-word funnel (COBOL0901, ProgramNameContext is a provable user-word position); WordCharacterScreen.CheckWord refuses the underscore and extended letters below 2002 (COBOL0900) and CharacterViolation an edge hyphen (COBOL2773). Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c): 31-char name both ends COBOL1567; END PROGRAM A_B COBOL0900 (accepted at 2023); MOVE COBOL0901; 123 and "ABC" COBOL5506; ABC- and -ABC COBOL2773; CAFÉ COBOL0900; END PROGRAM. COBOL0001; 1A and a 30-char name run. The witness's 31-char end-marker name gets COBOL1567 and COBOL2793.

next.reason: 1985: the END PROGRAM program-name 'must conform to the rules for forming a user-defined word', whose rules are §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 'A COBOL word is a character-string of not more than 30 characters ... selected from the set of letters, digits, and the hyphen'. 2023: program-name-1 of §2023:10.7.2, identical to the PROGRAM-ID name (§2023:10.7.3 SR2), is a user-defined word under §2023:8.3.2.1 SR1 (no reserved word) and §2023:8.3.2.2 SR3 (at least one letter), but §2023:8.3.2.1 now reads 'not more than 63 characters' with 'basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore'. END PROGRAM A_B, or a 31-63 character name, is refused by the 1985 rule and accepted by 2023: a widened range. The changed text is the 8.3.2.1 general paragraph, which has no catalog row (kb/Work PB479).
